question: In 2003, _____________ became the first Indian woman dancer to be awarded with the Padma Vibhushan.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonal Mansingh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2003**, Sonal Mansingh was awarded the **Padma Vibhushan**, India's second-highest civilian award, recognizing her contributions to Indian classical dance.
 
• She is renowned for her proficiency in **Bharatanatyam and Odissi**, two major classical dance forms of India.
 
• Beyond performance, Mansingh is also known for her efforts in dance education, choreography, and promoting Indian cultural heritage globally.
 
• Apart from the Padma Vibhushan, she has received numerous other awards, including the **Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Established in **1954**, the award is given for "**exceptional and distinguished service**" in any field including the **arts, education, industry, literature, science, sports, and social service**.
 
• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu, known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork, while Odissi is from Odisha, characterized by its fluid movements and expressive gestures.
 
• Sonal Mansingh has often been described as a cultural ambassador of India, using her performances to convey Indian mythology and folklore to international audiences.
 
• She has been actively involved in educational initiatives, conducting workshops and lectures that emphasize the role of dance in enhancing personal and social wellbeing.
